text: Configuration gives Oracle Fusion its rules; data migration gives it the actual legacy business history those rules operate on. This lesson covers how a Data Migration Lead decides what to migrate, how, and when, well before any file actually gets loaded.

Legacy data sorts into three categories. Static or reference data is master data every transaction depends on, like suppliers and bank accounts, loaded first. Open transactional balances are still-open items the business needs on day one: unpaid invoices, the GL trial balance at cutover. Historical data is closed transaction history kept for reporting only.

Most projects don't migrate full transaction history in detail. The business doesn't need to re-process a paid invoice from years ago, it just needs to know its balance was correct. So open balances get migrated in full detail, while historical data is left as summary reporting, often staying in the legacy system entirely.

Loading typically uses FBDI, a structured spreadsheet template per object, as the standard bulk mechanism. ADFdi handles smaller volumes or ongoing maintenance through Excel integration. Manual entry only works for very low volumes. REST APIs matter more for ongoing integrations than for a one-time conversion.

Brightfield's migration lead scopes Cash Management to all active bank, branch, and account records loaded first, every open reconciliation item as of cutover loaded via FBDI, and nothing from historical archives, which stay in the legacy system's reporting tool. Up next, lesson fifteen: cleansing and validating that data before and after it loads.
